newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SGB buys GBL's Tractebel stakes.
newsitem.headline: SGB buys GBL's Tractebel stakes.

text.p: Belgium's largest holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA put an end to weeks of speculation on Tuesday, announcing it would pay 49 billion Belgian francs to buy 24.47 percent in Tractebel from rival Belgian holding Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA (GBL).
After the transaction SGB will hold 65 percent in Tractebel, SGB chairman Etienne Davignon told a news conference.

It now has 40 percent in the Belgian energy and engineering holding company which controls the country's gas and electricity distribution companies as well as holding energy interests around the world.
SGB said it would also open up its 14,500 francs-a-share offer to other Tractebel shareholders.
"To avoid that this transaction leads to any discussion we have decided to offer to buy all Tractebel shares at 14,500 Belgian francs," the company said in a statement.
SGB plans to make a public offer for all shares from October 9 to 30, noting the Tractebel takeover was still subject to clearance from U.S. regulatory authorities.
SGB will also issue a put warrant on Tractebel shares, giving holders the right to sell their Tractebel shares to SGB at 14,500 francs in three years' time in November 1999.
"We guarantee investors that they can sell their shares at the same price in three years. The investor is taking no risk. We are taking all the risk because we believe in (Tractebel)," Davignon said.
Among other interests Tractebel controls Belgian electricity giant Electrabel, gas distributor Distrigas and international energy holding company Powerfin.
SGB, a unit of France's Cie de Suez, said it would pay for the acquisition using a combination of cash and newly negotiated credit lines.
SGB said that following the operation the weight of Tractebel in its portfolio would rise to around 40.7 percent from 27 percent.
GBL's interests in Tractebel were held for 20.38 percent through Belgian holding company Electrafina and for the rest via insurer Royale Belge.
Electrafina said the operation would boost its Treasury by 41 billion francs.
Royale Belge said it would make a capital gain of around four billion francs from the sale.
